author: Linsey Lewis
title: Fallen Las Vegas Metro officer was 'ambushed' by suspect in deadly east valley shooting: Sheriff - NewsBreak
text:
By Linsey Lewis ,
11 hours ago
LAS VEGAS (KLAS) — The Las Vegas Metro police officer killed in a shooting Tuesday, was “ambushed” by the suspect, Clark County Sheriff Kevin McMahill said during a press conference Wednesday.
On Tuesday, Aug. 4, Officer Austin Abdelnabi, 30, was killed in the line of duty while responding to a report of a person with a gun acting erratically and waving a firearm in the air at a business in the 4500 block of East Tropicana Avenue near I-11 and Mountain Vista Street.
Las Vegas police officer dies after shooting near Tropicana Avenue, I-11 Abdelnabi was a U.S. Marine veteran who had been with the department since November 2023. Abdelnabi had studied at Clemson University with a bachelor’s degree in criminal justice and law enforcement administration from 2018 to 2022, according to his LinkedIn page.
Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department Officer Austin Abdelnabi, 30, was killed in the line of duty on Tuesday, Aug. 4. (LVMPD) On Wednesday, Sheriff McMahill held a press conference where he discussed the shooting and provided details on who Officer Abdelnabi was.
“He worked in our Southeast Area Command, and he was known for his giant personality. Always laughing, even when his field training officers were ‘trying’ to provide him guidance,” McMahill said. “Austin was also known for talking about how much he loved his wife, Sage.”
Abdelnabi was born in South Carolina and was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. He was stationed at Camp Pendleton in California and was assigned to Weapons Company, Second Battalion, First Marine Division for his first deployment. He was a 50 caliber machine gun for his second deployment. He was deployed to Okinawa and Africa and was awarded the Marine Corps Good Conduct Medal, the National Defense Service Medal, the Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary Medal, and the Global War on Terrorism Service Medal, along with Sea Service Deployment Ribbons, according to McMahill.
Adbelnabi is survived by his wife, Sage, with whom he had been married to for eight years, his parents, two brothers, and his sister.
Shortly before 4 p.m. Tuesday, police received multiple reports, including a 911 call, that an armed suspect was walking acting erratically and waving a firearm in the air at a business in the area.
Full video: Procession for fallen LVMPD Officer Austin Abdelnabi When officers arrived, they located the armed individual near Mountain Vista Street
and the I-11 underpass.
McMahill said Wednesday that as Abdelnabi got out of his police vehicle, he was “ambushed” by the suspect.
A Las Vegas Metro police officer has died following a shooting in the east valley on Aug. 4, 2026. (Armando Navarro/KLAS) A Las Vegas Metro police officer has died following a shooting in the east valley. (KLAS) A Las Vegas Metro police officer has died following a shooting in the east valley on Aug. 4, 2026. (Armando Navarro/KLAS) Las Vegas Metro Police Department Sheriff Kevin McMahill did not identify the fallen officer by name but described him as a former Marine veteran who had been with the department since 2023. (KLAS) The suspect opened fire on police, and at least one officer returned fire, LVMPD Captain Adam Seely said late Tuesday during the second news conference of the night. Both the shooter and the officer were struck.
Officer Abdelnabi was injured and taken to a nearby hospital, where he was later pronounced dead, according to police.
Fallen Las Vegas police officer Austin Abdelnabi described as U.S. Marine veteran The suspect in the incident was also pronounced dead at the scene of the shooting.
“As you can imagine, I have a lot of grieving police officers and a grieving community,” McMahill said Tuesday. “I haven’t been to the scene yet. I came directly here to see our officer and his family.”
On Wednesday afternoon, a procession took Abdelnabi’s body from the Clark County Coroner’s Office to a local funeral home.
During the procession, members of Las Vegas law enforcement lined the streets where the hearse was driven, saluting the fallen officer.
Members of Las Vegas law enforcement salute as the procession for fallen Officer Austin Abdelnabi, 30, goes by. Abdelnabi was shot and killed on Aug. 4, 2026. (KLAS) Members of Las Vegas law enforcement salute as the procession for fallen Officer Austin Abdelnabi, 30, goes by. Abdelnabi was shot and killed on Aug. 4, 2026. (KLAS) The Nevada Police Foundation released several statements about the fallen officer.
“This incident illustrates the dangerous work police officers throughout this nation face daily,”
Adam Garcia, Executive Director of the Foundation, said. “Abdelnadi leaves a legacy of service and is a beacon of strength for all of us.”
“Officer Abdelnadi paid the ultimate price to ensure that Las Vegans could live in a safe community,” Michelle Bays, Chair of the Board of Directors of the Nevada Police Foundation, which is also the custodian of the Nevada Police Officer Memorial, added. “We will never forget his sacrifice. Our heavy hearts are with our law enforcement family at this difficult time.”
Clark County released a statement Wednesday saying:
“The Clark County family joins our community in mourning Officer Austin Abdelnabi. Our thoughts are with his loved ones and the men and women of LVMPD as they begin to process this tragic loss of life. Times like these can be challenging for many and the County reminds the public of trauma counseling resources available to them through the Resiliency & Justice Center. In tragedy, no one walks alone.”
President Donald Trump was in Las Vegas Wednesday at the Red Rock Hotel and Casino to tout his tax policies. When he took the stage, the president gave his condolences to the those affected by Abdelnabi’s loss, saying he died a hero.
8 News Now will have continuing coverage of Abdelnabi’s funeral, the investigation, and any other updates in this case on air, online and in the 8 News+ streaming app .
